name: @jointhewheel/mcp-server

tools.name: wheel_search
tools.description:
Search The Wheel knowledge base for relevant documents, patterns, and session history. Results are decrypted locally inside the MCP process using the entity key; plaintext content is never requested from the backend.

Args:
- query: Natural-language search query.
- tags: Optional tags to filter results.
- content_types: Optional content-type filters.
- limit: Maximum results to return, 1-50. Defaults to 10.
- response_format: 'markdown' for concise human-readable output or 'json' for structured text. The tool also returns structuredContent for capable clients.

Returns:
- results: Matching content snippets with IDs, titles, content types, tags, relevance scores, and truncation flags.
- metadata: total_count, count, latency_ms, and has_more.

Use when: you need to find relevant Wheel knowledge or historical context.
Do not use when: you need to list library metadata without decrypted snippets; use wheel_list_content instead.

response_format.description: Output format: 'markdown' for human-readable output or 'json' for complete structured text.

tools.name: wheel_list_content
tools.description:
List content in The Wheel knowledge base with pagination and filtering. Returns metadata only: title, type, tags, visibility, dates, and processing status. It does not decrypt or return content bodies.

Args:
- page: 1-based page number. Defaults to 1.
- limit: Items per page, 1-100. Defaults to 50.
- content_type: Optional content-type filter.
- tags: Optional tag filters.
- sort_by: date, name, type, or modified.
- sort_order: asc or desc.
- response_format: 'markdown' for human-readable output or 'json' for structured text. The tool also returns structuredContent for capable clients.

Returns:
- items: Content metadata rows.
- pagination: page, limit, total_count, total_pages, count, offset, has_more, and next_offset.

Use when: you need to browse or count content-library metadata.
Do not use when: you need decrypted matching snippets; use wheel_search instead.

content_type.description: Filter by content type such as note, document, email, conversation, task, or event

response_format.description: Output format: 'markdown' for human-readable output or 'json' for complete structured text.

tools.name: wheel_get_entity_info
tools.description:
Get the current user profile and entity information from The Wheel. Returns identity and scope metadata for the authenticated MCP session.

Args:
- response_format: 'markdown' for human-readable output or 'json' for structured text. The tool also returns structuredContent for capable clients.

Returns:
- id, email, display name, role, entity_id, and timezone.

Use when: you need to verify which Wheel user/entity this MCP server is authenticated as.
Do not use when: you need content search or content-library rows.

response_format.description: Output format: 'markdown' for human-readable output or 'json' for complete structured text.

tools.name: wheel_save_summary
tools.description:
Encrypt and save a connected-session summary to The Wheel. This is a write tool that encrypts locally with the entity key before upload.

Save only when the user asks to save this connected session. Supply a v2 session-memory object based on the visible conversation and observed tool results available to this host. A v2 save requires entity_level=false, personal_level=true, create_new (or omitted update_mode), and batch_summary (or omitted content_type). Do not include hidden reasoning, private filesystem paths, raw transcript excerpts, provider request payloads, or claims not supported by the visible session. State source scope honestly: use full_visible_conversation only when this host has the complete visible session; use partial_visible_conversation, explicit_host_summary, or tool_checkpoints otherwise. A tool-call checkpoint record is not a complete conversation summary. Mark an action attempted, reported_success, or observed_success according to its evidence; never infer completion from a proposed command. If the host lacks sufficient visible content, return needs_host_summary and do not save unless the caller explicitly requests a limited checkpoint record.

Args:
- title: Human-readable summary title.
- summary_version: Set to v2 when session_memory is supplied; omit for the legacy v1 shape.
- session_memory: Strict wheel.session_memory.v2 object. It cannot be combined with summary, structured_summary, or transcript_evidence.
- summary, structured_summary, transcript_evidence: Legacy v1 inputs retained for compatibility.
- content_id: Deprecated create compatibility hint. Wheel generates IDs by default; updates use update_handle.
- update_mode: For v2, omit or use create_new. Legacy v1 may use update_existing with update_handle.
- content_type: For v2, omit or use batch_summary. Legacy v1 defaults to batch_summary.
- entity_level: For v2, explicitly set false. Legacy v1 defaults to true.
- personal_level: For v2, explicitly set true. Legacy v1 defaults from MCP setup.
- response_format: markdown or json.

Returns:
- Existing success, saved, quality, review, searchable-state, next-action, and update-handle fields.
- A receipt that states acceptance, disposition, coverage, capture boundary, review state, and item handle without claiming indexing or answer eligibility.

Use when: the user explicitly asks to save connected-session context.
Do not use when: answering read-only questions, importing historical archives, or when the host cannot state its visible-session coverage honestly.

title.description: Host-facing summary title. The local MCP process encrypts this before backend upload.

encrypted_title.description: Advanced: pre-encrypted metadata title. Prefer title unless you have already used Wheel metadata encryption.

content_id.description: Deprecated compatibility hint. Create paths use Wheel-generated IDs; update paths require update_handle.

update_handle.description: Opaque handle returned by a previous save; required for update_existing.

update_mode.description: For v2, omit or use create_new; update_existing is legacy v1 only and requires update_handle.

content_type.description: For v2, omit or use batch_summary. Legacy v1 also defaults to batch_summary.

tags.description: Deprecated plaintext tag labels. D48 rejects these before backend upload; use tag_ids from MCP settings.

tag_ids.description: Encrypted tag vocabulary IDs selected through Wheel MCP settings.

summary_version.description: Set to v2 only when session_memory contains a strict wheel.session_memory.v2 object.

session_memory.description: Strict wheel.session_memory.v2 object. Valid only with summary_version=v2.

structured_summary.description: Structured host-authored session memory for the legacy v1 path.

decisions.description: Decisions made during the connected session.

actions.description: Actions completed or attempted during the connected session.

artifacts.description: Artifacts, files, branches, PRs, commands, or references touched.

transcript_evidence.description: Bounded transcript/excerpt evidence encrypted inside the summary payload.

sourceType.description: Evidence source category supplied by the local MCP host.

sourceId.description: Opaque local source identifier; never treated as backend authorization.

sourceLabel.description: User-facing local label stored only inside the encrypted content payload.

excerptText.description: Plaintext evidence excerpt encrypted inside the summary payload.

timestampStart.description: Optional ISO timestamp or host offset.

timestampEnd.description: Optional ISO timestamp or host offset.

contentHash.description: Local SHA-256 or equivalent hash of normalized excerpt text.

summary.description: Backward-compatible host-authored narrative. If omitted, generated from MCP tool-call checkpoints only.

entity_level.description: For v2, explicitly set false. Legacy v1 defaults to true.

personal_level.description: For v2, explicitly set true. Legacy v1 defaults from the MCP setup summary target.

response_format.description: Output format: 'markdown' for human-readable output or 'json' for complete structured text.

tools.name: wheel_logout
tools.description:
Log out of the Wheel MCP server by clearing local credentials and session state. This does not delete Wheel account data or knowledge-base content.

Args:
- response_format: 'markdown' for human-readable output or 'json' for structured text. The tool also returns structuredContent for capable clients.

Returns:
- success and message.

Use when: the user explicitly asks to disconnect or remove local MCP credentials.
Do not use when: answering read-only questions or evaluating content.

response_format.description: Output format: 'markdown' for human-readable output or 'json' for complete structured text.
